data.train_batch_size.impact: Number of prompts in one training update; changes total work and data-parallel scheduling more than single-kernel peak memory.
data.train_batch_size.increase: More work per update and potentially better amortization, but longer steps and more rollout samples.
data.train_batch_size.decrease: Shorter updates with noisier measurements and potentially lower utilization.
constraints: train_batch_size * rollout.n must be divisible by ppo_mini_batch_size
hardware comparisons preserve the total token budget

data.max_prompt_length.impact: Maximum prompt tokens; affects prefill compute, activations, KV cache, and padded work.
data.max_prompt_length.increase: Raises rollout and log-prob memory/latency, especially without remove padding.
data.max_prompt_length.decrease: Lowers pressure but changes the workload unless compensated under the token-budget rule.
constraints: Must match dataset truncation policy
hardware token budget is frozen

data.max_response_length.impact: Maximum generated tokens; strongly affects decode time, KV cache, log-prob, and actor-training activations.
data.max_response_length.increase: Raises all four phase costs and makes rollout more likely to dominate.
data.max_response_length.decrease: Reduces memory/time but changes the RL workload unless budget is preserved.
constraints: hardware token budget is frozen

actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz.impact: Uses token-aware dynamic micro batches instead of fixed sample counts.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz.increase: Can improve packing and reduce padding variance, but changes which fixed micro-batch settings are authoritative.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz.decrease: Makes fixed per-GPU micro batches directly control work.
constraints: Verify the selected verl backend supports the dynamic-batch fields

actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_.impact: Per-GPU fixed PPO update micro batch; controls training activation memory, gradient-accumulation work, and kernel utilization.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_.increase: May improve training utilization and reduce gradient-accumulation iterations when the current micro batch is too small and training memory has headroom; otherwise it can raise the training peak or cause OOM without improving step time.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_.decrease: Reduces training activation pressure and is the first local control for training OOM, but adds gradient-accumulation iterations and can lower utilization.
constraints: Positive integer
Only authoritative when actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz is false
The backend-normalized local PPO mini batch must be divisible by this per-GPU micro batch
Changing actor TP or PP requires revalidating the legal micro-batch values

actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_s.impact: PPO mini-batch size per update; controls optimization grouping and the number of PPO mini batches.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_s.increase: Changes optimization granularity and may reduce loop overhead, but is not the main per-kernel memory control.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_s.decrease: Creates more mini-batch partitions and may increase overhead.
constraints: train_batch_size * rollout.n must be divisible by it
it must be divisible by ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.tensor_.impact: Shards actor training tensor computation and model states across ranks; it is a topology control rather than a monotonic throughput knob.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.tensor_.increase: Reduces per-rank model and activation pressure, but adds tensor-parallel collectives and can reduce throughput when communication is already significant.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.tensor_.decrease: Reduces tensor-parallel communication and may improve kernels, but increases per-rank memory and can become infeasible.
constraints: Positive integer
world size must be divisible by actor TP * PP
Changing TP changes data-parallel size and requires revalidating backend-normalized PPO mini/micro batching

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pipelin.impact: Partitions actor training layers into pipeline stages; it trades per-rank model memory for pipeline bubbles, transfers, and scheduling complexity.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pipelin.increase: Reduces layers and model-state memory per rank, but usually adds pipeline bubbles and inter-stage communication; it is mainly useful when actor memory does not fit with lower PP.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pipelin.decrease: Reduces pipeline overhead and often improves training efficiency when memory fits, but increases per-rank model memory.
constraints: Positive integer
world size must be divisible by actor TP * PP
Changing PP changes data-parallel size and requires revalidating backend-normalized PPO mini/micro batching

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.sequenc.impact: Shards eligible actor training sequence-dimension activations within tensor-parallel groups.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.sequenc.enable: Can lower training activation memory when TP is greater than one and sequences are long, but adds sequence-parallel collective communication.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.sequenc.disable: Avoids sequence-parallel collectives and may improve training throughput when activation memory is not limiting, but increases replicated activation memory.
constraints: Backend kernels must support sequence parallelism
Normally useful only when actor TP > 1
Evaluate it together with actor TP rather than as an independent monotonic knob

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_dis.impact: Shards optimizer states and related buffers across data-parallel ranks.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_dis.increase: Reduces training optimizer memory with communication/bookkeeping cost.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_dis.decrease: Replicates more optimizer state and may simplify execution.
constraints: Requires compatible Megatron/distributed backend

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_rem.impact: Removes padded tokens from actor computation when supported.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_rem.increase: Reduces wasted compute and memory for variable-length samples.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.use_rem.decrease: Uses regular padded shapes, which may be simpler but wasteful.
constraints: Validate kernel/backend compatibility

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.optimiz.impact: Moves actor optimizer states away from GPU between/within training operations.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.optimiz.increase: Lowers training GPU memory but adds host/device transfer latency.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.optimiz.decrease: Keeps optimizer state on GPU for speed at higher memory cost.
constraints: Host memory must be sufficient

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.param_o.impact: Moves actor parameters away from GPU when inactive.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.param_o.increase: Creates headroom for rollout/ref phases but adds reload transfer time.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.param_o.decrease: Keeps parameters resident for faster phase transitions at higher memory use.
constraints: Host memory and transfer bandwidth must be sufficient

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.impact: Selects activation recomputation scope, commonly full or selective.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.increase: Stronger recomputation lowers training activation memory and increases compute.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.decrease: Stores more activations for faster backward at higher peak memory.
constraints: Values must be supported by the installed Megatron version

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.impact: Selects transformer submodules included in selective recomputation.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.increase: More modules reduce saved activations but add repeated forward work.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.decrease: Less repeated compute but higher activation memory.
constraints: Module names are backend-version specific; search local verl/Megatron docs first

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.impact: Controls how recomputation is distributed across transformer layers.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.increase: Method choice shifts the memory/compute pattern across layers.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.decrease: No universal monotonic direction; compare supported uniform/block behavior.
constraints: Must match backend-supported enum values

actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.impact: Number or grouping of layers recomputed under the selected method.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.increase: Usually lowers stored activation memory and raises repeated compute.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.overrid.decrease: Usually improves speed while consuming more activation memory.
constraints: Meaning depends on recompute_method and Megatron version

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_p.impact: Shards rollout model execution, weights, and KV-cache-related state across ranks; it trades per-rank memory for per-token tensor-parallel communication.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_p.increase: Reduces per-rank weight and cache pressure and may make larger scheduler batches feasible, but adds communication to generation and can reduce decode throughput.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_p.decrease: Reduces per-token communication and may improve rollout throughput when the model and KV cache fit, but raises per-rank memory pressure.
constraints: Positive integer
world size must be divisible by rollout TP
Compare measured rollout throughput and memory rather than assuming either direction is faster
Avoid changing rollout TP and scheduler caps in the same trial unless restoring feasibility

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro.impact: Per-GPU fixed micro batch for actor old-log-prob computation; despite its rollout config path, it affects the actor_log_prob phase rather than token generation.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro.increase: May improve actor_log_prob utilization and reduce forward-pass iterations when that phase is significant and memory has headroom, but raises its activation peak.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro.decrease: Reduces actor_log_prob activation pressure and is useful for phase-specific OOM, but adds forward-pass iterations and may lower utilization.
constraints: Positive integer
Validate the installed backend's local batching and divisibility semantics

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_uti.impact: Fraction of GPU memory exposed as a rollout-engine memory budget, primarily for model execution and KV-cache capacity; it is not the measured GPU compute-utilization percentage.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_uti.increase: Raises the rollout memory budget and may permit more cache capacity or concurrency when memory capacity is the binding limit, but reduces safety headroom and can cause initialization/runtime OOM.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_uti.decrease: Creates memory safety headroom, but may reduce cache capacity, concurrency, and rollout throughput when the budget is already binding.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_uti.tuning_strategies: Call analyze_rollout_metrics on a comparable trial. Increase only when KV-cache usage or preemption demonstrates capacity pressure and phase-specific physical memory has safe headroom; never use low GPU compute utilization alone.
constraints: Agent range 0.1-0.95
Treat it as a memory-capacity control, not a direct GPU-utilization target
Estimate effects from comparable trial history because the realized reservation is backend dependent

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batche.impact: Upper bound on tokens admitted to one rollout scheduler batch; it is a capacity ceiling, not a request to allocate that many tokens every iteration.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batche.increase: Can improve prefill/decode packing only when the current token cap is binding and pending work exists; otherwise it may have no throughput effect while allowing higher temporary memory pressure.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batche.decrease: Reduces scheduler-batch memory pressure and may avoid OOM or long oversized batches, but adds scheduling waves when the cap was binding.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batche.tuning_strategies: Call analyze_rollout_metrics. Increase only when exported iteration-token statistics approach this cap while requests remain queued and KV/physical memory have headroom; if the exporter omits iteration-token metrics, treat the cap as unobserved and use an isolated comparison trial.
constraints: Positive integer
Must support viable request shapes for the configured sequence lengths
Confirm from rollout logs or trial comparisons that the token cap is binding before optimizing it

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_seqs.impact: Upper bound on concurrent sequences admitted by the rollout scheduler; it limits scheduler concurrency but does not guarantee that many runnable sequences.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_seqs.increase: Can improve batching and device utilization only when the current sequence cap is binding and enough requests are pending; otherwise it may have no effect while permitting more KV-cache and scheduler state.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_seqs.decrease: Reduces concurrency-related memory pressure and may improve stability, but can underfill the device and increase rollout duration when the cap was binding.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_seqs.tuning_strategies: Call analyze_rollout_metrics. Increase only when requests_running reaches this cap while requests_waiting remains positive and KV/physical memory have headroom. A token-length ratio is only a feasibility heuristic, not proof that the sequence cap is binding.
constraints: Positive integer
Confirm from rollout logs or trial comparisons that the sequence cap is binding before optimizing it

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.disable_log_st.impact: Controls whether vLLM exposes/logs runtime statistics used by the rollout monitor. It is an observability switch, not a throughput-tuning parameter.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.disable_log_st.enable: Set to false before the experiment to allow automatic collection of compact vLLM metrics.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.disable_log_st.disable: When true or absent, the automatic vLLM monitor does not start because scheduler/KV statistics are not considered available.
constraints: Must be explicitly false to start the vLLM monitor
Do not propose changing it as a performance experiment
It remains outside the editable tuning whitelist

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.free_cache_eng.impact: Releases rollout cache-engine memory when moving to other colocated phases.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.free_cache_eng.increase: Creates actor/ref/training headroom but adds cache teardown/recreation overhead.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.free_cache_eng.decrease: Improves phase transition speed while keeping more rollout memory resident.
constraints: Behavior depends on rollout backend

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked.impact: Splits long prompt prefills into scheduler chunks.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked.increase: Reduces single-prefill peaks and can mix prefill/decode work, with scheduling overhead.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked.decrease: Uses simpler full prefills that may peak higher for long prompts.
constraints: Requires rollout-backend support

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_prefix_.impact: Caches reusable prompt prefixes in rollout KV state.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_prefix_.increase: Speeds repeated prefixes but retains cache entries and adds bookkeeping.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_prefix_.decrease: Avoids cache retention when prompts do not share useful prefixes.
constraints: Benefit depends on actual prefix reuse

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager.impact: Forces eager rollout execution instead of graph-based execution where available.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager.increase: Often improves compatibility and reduces graph-capture memory, but can lower throughput.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager.decrease: Allows graph optimizations with capture/startup memory and backend constraints.
constraints: Use the installed rollout backend's semantics

actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.tensor_mo.impact: Shards reference-model forward computation and states across ranks; it trades ref_log_prob memory for tensor-parallel communication.
actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.tensor_mo.increase: Reduces per-rank reference-model and activation pressure, but adds collectives and can slow ref_log_prob when memory was already sufficient.
actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.tensor_mo.decrease: Reduces collective communication and may improve ref_log_prob throughput when the model fits, but raises per-rank memory pressure.
constraints: Positive integer
world size must be divisible by ref TP * PP
Prioritize this only when ref_log_prob time or memory pressure is material

actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.pipeline_.impact: Partitions reference-model layers into pipeline stages; it mainly trades per-rank model memory for pipeline bubbles and transfers in ref_log_prob.
actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.pipeline_.increase: Reduces reference-model layers and memory per rank, but adds pipeline overhead; it is mainly useful when ref memory does not fit with lower PP.
actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.pipeline_.decrease: Reduces pipeline overhead and may improve ref_log_prob efficiency when memory fits, but raises per-rank model memory.
constraints: Positive integer
world size must be divisible by ref TP * PP
Prioritize this only when ref_log_prob time or memory pressure is material

actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.sequence_.impact: Shards eligible reference-model sequence activations within tensor-parallel groups during ref_log_prob.
actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.sequence_.enable: Can lower reference activation memory when ref TP is greater than one and sequences are long, but adds sequence-parallel collective communication.
actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.sequence_.disable: Avoids sequence-parallel collectives and may improve ref_log_prob throughput when activation memory is not limiting, but increases replicated activation memory.
constraints: Backend kernels must support sequence parallelism
Normally useful only when ref TP > 1
Prioritize this only when ref_log_prob time or memory pressure is material

actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.param_off.impact: Offloads inactive reference-model parameters from GPU.
actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.param_off.increase: Reduces cross-phase resident memory but adds reload transfers.
actor_rollout_ref.ref.megatron.param_off.decrease: Keeps ref parameters resident for speed at higher GPU memory cost.
constraints: Host memory and bandwidth must be sufficient

actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_bat.impact: Per-GPU fixed micro batch for reference log-prob forward passes; it directly controls ref_log_prob activation pressure and iteration count.
actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_bat.increase: May improve ref_log_prob utilization and reduce forward-pass iterations when that phase is significant and memory has headroom, but raises its activation peak.
actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_bat.decrease: Reduces ref_log_prob activation pressure and is useful for phase-specific OOM, but adds forward-pass iterations and may lower utilization.
constraints: Positive integer
Only authoritative when actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz is false
Validate the installed backend's local batching and divisibility semantics

actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr.impact: Actor optimizer learning rate; a primary RL update-size and stability control.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr.increase: Can learn faster but raises KL/clip pressure and collapse risk.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr.decrease: Usually improves stability but may slow reward improvement.
constraints: Agent range 1e-7 to 1e-5

actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr_warmup_.impact: Number of initial optimizer steps used to ramp the learning rate.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr_warmup_.increase: Reduces early shocks but delays full learning rate.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr_warmup_.decrease: Reaches target LR sooner with more startup instability risk.
constraints: Warmup must be meaningfully smaller than the evaluation horizon

actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss.impact: Enables an explicit actor KL penalty in the optimization loss.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss.increase: Constrains policy drift when coefficient/type are configured.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss.decrease: Removes this loss constraint; reward-side KL is a separate mechanism.
constraints: Do not confuse loss KL with reward KL

actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef.impact: Weight of the actor KL loss.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef.increase: Restrains policy drift but can suppress reward learning.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef.decrease: Allows larger policy updates with greater KL risk.
constraints: Has effect only when use_kl_loss is true
Agent range 0-0.2

actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type.impact: Estimator/formulation used for KL loss; changes numerical behavior and variance.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type.increase: No monotonic direction; select based on installed verl semantics and observed KL behavior.
constraints: Search local verl source for supported enum values before changing

actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff.impact: Weight of entropy regularization in the actor objective.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff.increase: Encourages exploration but may weaken task-reward optimization.
actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff.decrease: Makes updates more reward-directed and may reduce diversity.
constraints: Agent range 0-0.2; diagnose entropy behavior before changing

actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n.impact: Number of responses sampled per prompt for GRPO grouping.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n.increase: Provides more within-prompt comparisons but increases rollout/token work and can affect variance.
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n.decrease: Reduces rollout cost but weakens group statistics.
constraints: train_batch_size * n must be divisible by ppo_mini_batch_size
Changing n changes workload and requires careful end-to-end comparison
